cards.text: Israel is camped out, tribe by tribe, and the LORD has a word for Moses. This one's about who stays inside the camp and who has to be sent outside. Listen close, friend, because God is VERY specific here.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to send certain people away from the camp. Which of these is one of them?
The LORD says only the men in these groups have to be sent outside the camp.
Why does the LORD want these people sent outside the camp?

answers.text: So they won't defile the camp where He dwells
So the tribes can march out in order
So the Levites can finish their count

cards.question: When the LORD gives this command, the Israelites do just as He instructed Moses.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again. New topic: what happens when a man or woman sins against another person.

cards.question: When someone sins against another person, they act unfaithfully against the ___.
That person is guilty. What's the first thing the guilty person must do?

answers.text: Leave the camp for a week

cards.question: After confessing, he must make full restitution. What does he add on top of it?

cards.text: A FIFTH on top! Friend, if you knock five cookies off my counter, you don't bring me back five. You bring me back SIX. That's not just sorry. That's sorry with INTEREST.

cards.question: All of this payment goes to the person he wronged.

cards.text: But here's a curveball. What if there's no relative to receive the payment for the wrong? Does the guilty guy just slide that money back in his pocket and whistle? Not so fast.

cards.question: With no relative to pay back, the restitution belongs to the ___.
That restitution is given to the priest along with a ram of atonement.

cards.text: Then the LORD adds one last word, about the sacred gifts the Israelites bring to the priest.

cards.question: Every sacred contribution the Israelites bring to the priest belongs to ___.
Before a man gives his sacred gifts to the priest, they still belong to the man.

findings.problem: The card cites only Numbers 5:1. It also uses 5:2-3 ("who has to be sent outside" the camp). "Camped out, tribe by tribe" is a fact from outside the passage (Numbers 2) and has no reference.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Tribe by tribe" comes from Numbers 2, outside the passage, and has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: No card ever tells the other two groups in Numbers 5:2: anyone with a bodily discharge and anyone defiled by a dead body. The baker learns only about skin disease, then gets asked about "these groups" on cards 3 and 4.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "These groups" points back to groups the baker can't see on screen and was never fully told.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer is noticeably longer than the two wrong answers and sounds more like the Bible ("defile," "where He dwells"), so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to the fifth answered on card 9. It tells no new part of the passage, so it works as a joke-only recap.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Numbers 5:7-8 calls it restitution, not money. "Slide that money back in his pocket" states as part of the retelling that the restitution is money, which the text doesn't say.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
